title: Belling the Cat

sentences.text: The mice in an old house called a meeting inside the wall.
A cat had been stalking the kitchen, and every errand had become dangerous.
One mouse stood up and said they should tie a bell to the cat's collar.
Then we will hear the cat coming and slip away in time, the mouse added.
The other mice cheered. The plan sounded clever and simple.
An old mouse, who had not cheered, waited until the noise faded.
The bell is a fine idea, said the old mouse. Who is going to put it on the cat?
Silence filled the wall. Nobody wanted that job.
They looked at the floor, at their paws, and at the crack that led toward the kitchen.
A plan can sound perfect until someone has to carry out the dangerous part.
The mice still needed a safer habit, so they agreed to post a lookout by the crack.
It was a smaller idea, but it was an idea someone could actually do.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A clever plan that nobody can safely carry out
A cat who asks to wear a new collar
A kitchen that is rebuilt for mice
An old mouse who loves loud bells

questions.explanation: The bell sounds clever until the old mouse asks who will put it on the cat. Nobody can do the dangerous part. That is the main idea.

questions.prompt: What question does the old mouse ask?

choices.text: Who will cook supper for the cat?
Who is going to put the bell on the cat?
Where did the mice buy the bell?
When will the wall be painted?

questions.explanation: After the cheering, the old mouse asks who is going to put the bell on the cat. The silence that follows is the answer.

questions.prompt: The cat had been stalking the kitchen. What does stalking mean?

choices.text: Ringing a bell as a warning
Following quietly in order to catch

questions.explanation: Stalking means following quietly in order to catch something. The cat makes every mouse errand dangerous, which fits that meaning.

questions.prompt: What do the mice decide last?

choices.text: To cheer for the bell plan
To call a meeting in the wall
To ask who will bell the cat
To post a lookout by the crack

questions.explanation: The meeting and the bell idea come first. After nobody will do that job, the last decision is to post a lookout by the crack.

attribution: A retelling of a public-domain fable by Aesop. The wording is original, and the lookout idea was added for this version.
